newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Nov 22.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Nov 22.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Friday morning:
NEWS OUTLOOK:
** Gloom sets in as onslaught of disappointing first-half profit announcements continues. Earnings announcements expected today include Larsen & Toubro, TVS Suzuki, IPCL, Vysya Bank and VSNL
** Shares of IDBI expected to be hit after firm's first half results announced on Thursday fall sharply below market expectations

** Supply of natural gas on the Hazira-Bijapur-Jagdishpur (HBJ) pipeline is being curtailed from November 25 to December 17, the Economic Times newspaper reports. Fertiliser companies and power plants located along the pipeline, based on natural gas as feedstock, will face supply cut ranging from 50-60 percent, the paper says
** A delay in the hike of petroleum prices will lead to a doubling of the subsidy on petroleum products this year, the Business Standard newspaper reports
The subsidy on petroleum products is expected to touch a staggering 184.4 billion rupees against 93.6 billion in fiscal 1995/96 (April-March), the paper says.

** Market regulator the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) is planning a sophisticated Stock Watch System similar to those in developed markets. The Stock Watch System would detect abuses such as market manipulation and insider trading, the Business Line newspaper reports
SEBI has asked all stock exchanges to maintain a weekly cap of 25 percent in the band for scrips that are traded above par in order to check abnormal price variations of traded scrips, the paper says
** Indian rupee INR= opens at 35.70/71 per dollar against Thursday's close of 35.69/70. Traders say rupee expected to gain on poor demand for the U.S. currency

** Study by securities firm Dil Vikas Finance Ltd finds first half results of Indian firms announced so far have shown modest 4.0 percent growth in net profit and a 2.1 percent fall in earnings. The study included a sample of 181 firms which announced results until November 19.
MARKETS:
** Benchmark BSE 30-share index slides 19.20 pts to 3043.30 on Thursday
** National Stock Exchange index down 6.79 points to 869.82
** James Capel Indian GDR index closes 1.43 points or 2.31 percent lower at 60.46 with the premium over the local market at 15.75 percent against 17.66 on Wednesday
STOCKS TO WATCH:
** General Motors Corp.'s Delphi Interior & Lighting Systems unit said Thursday it recently approved the expansion of its Sung San Co Ltd lighting joint venture into India
Sung San, located in Taegu, South Korea, is a joint venture between Delphi Interior & Lighting and Sam Lip Industrial Co and designs and manufactures auto lighting products
Sung San will be part of a new joint venture in Noida, India, with Fiem Industries Ltd and DCM Daewoo Motors Ltd.

** Global aluminium giant Aluminium Pechiney of France is likely to be the new foreign collaborator of Indian engineering major Larsen & Toubro Ltd in the latter's proposed one million tonne alumina project in Orissa, the Financial Express newspaper reports
